source_label: Diablo Weather Labs · Nov 19 4 PM briefing (3:55 PM PT) + NWS Bay Area AFD (1:54 PM PT) and NWS Sacramento AFD (12:40 PM PT) + latest local HRRR/RRFS/ECMWF/GFS and EPS/GEFS guidance

Moraga.headline: The storm is pulling east, but one more shower window remains before a colder weekend
Moraga.text: After 1.13 inches at KCAMORAG71 today, the heaviest rain has shifted away from Moraga and the evening should turn quieter. The local model blend brings another shower chance toward daybreak Friday, with a few showers possibly lingering into the afternoon; thunder chances have fallen below five percent as the upper low moves inland. Friday stays cool, with another chilly start Saturday before a weaker front brings spotty weekend rain. A more substantial, still uncertain system is taking shape for Tuesday into Wednesday.

Lafayette.headline: Reliez Valley gets a breather, but scattered showers may return before Friday is done
Lafayette.text: Reliez Valley catches a quieter evening after another soaking, but scattered showers can still return toward Friday morning. The local blend keeps a modest early-day shower signal, and the NWS still allows showers to linger into Friday afternoon; the thunder threat is now very low as the low moves inland. Friday will stay several degrees below seasonal averages, and a weaker front may bring another round of light, uneven rain Saturday into Sunday. A potentially wetter system approaches Tuesday–Wednesday, though its track and local totals remain uncertain.

Danville.headline: Sycamore Valley sees the main storm depart, with a few showers still in the wings
Danville.text: The main rain band is shifting away from Sycamore Valley, leaving a quieter evening, though a few showers may redevelop toward daybreak Friday. Local guidance keeps Friday's rain lighter than today's soaking, and the Bay Area thunder risk is now very low as the upper low moves inland. Expect a cool Friday with some brighter breaks, then a weaker, uneven round of rain over the weekend, with Monday offering the best pause. Forecast confidence falls again Tuesday–Wednesday, when a stronger Pacific system could bring more widespread rain.

Greenbrook.headline: Greenbrook gets a lull tonight, but the unsettled pattern is not finished
Greenbrook.text: Greenbrook should get a lull this evening as the storm's center tracks northeast, but don't put the umbrella away just yet. The local blend still supports a few showers early Friday, with scattered activity possibly lingering into the afternoon; thunder chances are now below five percent as the upper low moves inland. A weaker front may brush the Danville valley late Saturday into Sunday, then a stronger system could bring renewed rain Tuesday–Wednesday, although timing and totals remain unsettled.

Marin City.headline: Cool bay air and a few lingering showers keep Marin City unsettled
Marin City.text: Marin City's near-bay setting stays cool and breezy as the last coastal showers taper, with another passing shower possible overnight into Friday. The nearby coastal model blend keeps Friday's rainfall light, while west-to-northwest flow and lingering cloud cover limit any meaningful warm-up. A Bay Shoreline Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect through Saturday morning, so low-lying waterfront spots deserve attention around high tide. A weaker front may add showers this weekend, ahead of a potentially wetter Tuesday–Wednesday system.

Sausalito.headline: Sausalito's waterfront stays showery, with another wet pulse possible this weekend
Sausalito.text: Sausalito's waterfront will stay breezy, with temperatures more moderated than inland valleys, as scattered showers ease this evening but another shower window remains possible before Friday afternoon. The local blend holds a stronger early-Friday signal here than farther inland, then a weak front brings a better chance of rain Saturday into Sunday. A Bay Shoreline Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect through Saturday morning, and high tides deserve extra attention around low-lying waterfront areas. A potentially wetter Pacific system may arrive Tuesday–Wednesday, though its exact track is still uncertain.

Brentwood.headline: The Delta dries out tonight, but a stray storm and lingering flood concerns remain
Brentwood.text: The Delta side of East County is drying out faster this evening as the storm's low pulls northeast, but a stray shower or thunderstorm cannot be ruled out through early evening. Any cell could briefly bring a downpour, lightning or a gusty burst, although local model probabilities have dropped sharply since this afternoon. The Flood Advisory remains in effect for low-lying Delta areas until 4:45 PM Friday, so watch drainage channels and ponded roads. A weaker weekend system brings lighter rain, before a more organized Pacific system may renew the rain Tuesday–Wednesday.

East Sacramento.headline: East Sacramento's rain eases tonight, with a cooler Friday and another system ahead
East Sacramento.text: East Sacramento has seen the steadier rain shift east with the low, and the evening should be mostly quieter, though a stray shower remains possible nearby. The local blend keeps a modest shower chance into Friday morning, then favors a cooler day with brighter breaks; those inland intervals may warm faster than the coast before temperatures drop quickly after sunset. A weaker system brings another light rain chance late Saturday into Sunday, followed by a relative lull Monday. The next stronger Pacific system may reach the Valley Tuesday–Wednesday, but its track and rainfall totals are still uncertain.
